To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electron transfer process across the NTM/Mg 2+/MPA/Au surface is dependent on the complexation of the NTMP and their corresponding ΔEgap.
the ET kinetics across nucleobases terminated self-assembled film is dependent on the complexation of the NTMP with the Mg and their corresponding ΔE gap.

Mg-NTMPs have been successfully immobilized on gold electrode surface, and the ET kinetics of Mg-NTMP across the nucleobase terminated self-assembled film were investigated and the results were correlated with the Δ E gap of the corresponding Mg-NTMPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electron transfer across the nucleobase terminated self-assembled monolayer film.
the study on the electron transfer process across the nucleotides terminated surface, which is of great significance in the development of biosensors and bioelectronics.

the ET kinetics across the nucleobase terminated multilayer film, which is helpful for the understanding of the ET kinetics across nucleobase modified electrode and may be helpful for the design of the biosensor based on nucleobase modified electrodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ET kinetics across the self-assembled film is determined not only by the complexation of metal with nucleobases, but also the energy gaps of their corresponding metal-nucleobases complexes.
the rate of electron transfer across the NTMP terminated multilayer film is mainly controlled by the Δ E gap of their corresponding Mg 2+ -NTMP complexes.
the rate of the electron transfer kinetics is mainly controlled by the complexation of the Mg 2+ with the nucleotide monophosphates (NTMP), and their corresponding ΔEgap.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the complexation between Mg 2+ with the nucleobase, and the corresponding Δ E gap of their complex motif may play important role for ET process across the NTM/Mg 2+/MPA/Au film.
the electron transfer kinetics across the nucleobase terminated self-assembled film can be controlled by the complexation of nucleotide with metal cation and the corresponding Δ E gap.
Mg-NTMP complex motif may act as an ET relay in the nucleobases self-assembled film and the ET kinetics across NTMP terminated self-assembled film may be affected by the complexation of NTMP with Mg.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mg-NTMP motifs may be a good candidate for constructing the molecular wires in the molecular electronics and the molecular devices.
the ET rate of NTMP/Mg ^{2+} /MPA/Augate film can be modulated by changing the nucleobases, which is of significance to design and develop nucleic acid-based biosensors.
the nucleobases self-assembled films could be a potential candidate for constructing biosensor.
